pictures.text: [[tierc:legend|default:none]] Today the flame would leave Candlemere, in the old brass Keepers' Lantern. [[block:pic3.p2.gp]]

image.light: warm honey hearth light, afternoon sun through the window

figures.doing: holding the brass lantern near the fire, its little door open

props: the Keepers' Lantern, little door open
image.ember: sitting by the log basket, ears up
image.comfort_in_frame: the grandparent right beside the children

pictures.text: "Please," whispered [[block:pic3.small]]. Everyone waited in a hush…and the flame hopped across. The whole lantern glowed like a jar of honey.

image.light: warm honey hearth light, afternoon sun through the window, and now the lantern's gold glow

figures.doing: holding the lantern by the fire

props: a small gold flame hopping from the hearth into the lantern's chimney
image.ember: peeking out from behind the log basket
image.comfort_in_frame: everyone close together at the hearth

image.light: warm honey hearth light, afternoon sun through the window

figures.doing: showing a slow breath, lips soft

props: the lit lantern on the table, closed
image.ember: trying the breath too, looking very pleased
image.comfort_in_frame: everyone sitting close on the rug

pictures.text: Names were scratched on the lantern's base, and one was worn smooth. [[block:pic3.p10.gp]] Ember looked at it for a long time, and said nothing.

image.light: warm honey hearth light, afternoon sun through the window

figures.doing: holding the lantern upside down, thumb on one smooth place

props: tiny scratched marks on the lantern's base, too small to read
image.ember: very still, gazing at the smooth place

pictures.text: [[block:pic3.p13.gp]] Off went everyone, with [[child:eldest]] carrying the lantern as steady as steady.

image.setting: the cottage gate, the road running west between hedges
image.light: late afternoon on the road, low gold sun

figures.doing: carrying the shut lantern by its ring
waving, red wool on knitting needles

props: a red scarf just cast on
image.ember: trotting ahead, tail up like a flag
image.comfort_in_frame: the grandparent at the gate behind them

pictures.text: All afternoon the road ran west, and Ember stepped round every puddle. Soon Candlemere was only a smudge of roofs. Nobody said so, but everyone looked back once. [[tierc:jar_credit|default:none]]

image.setting: the Keepers' Way between hedges full of rosehips, grey milestones, the village small behind

figures.doing: carrying the shut lantern, looking back

pictures.text: At sunset everyone passed a hollow oak, as wide as a doorway. Far ahead stood a shepherd's hut. Then *whoo*, the wind rose, and the flame shrank to a tiny blue bead.

image.setting: the open road, a hollow oak at the roadside, a small hut far ahead
image.light: sunset going to dusk; the lantern's tiny blue glow
props: the lantern with a tiny blue flame
image.ember: tail blown sideways, ears back at the wind

pictures.text: [[child:eldest]]'s heart thumped in the dark. Then [[child:eldest]] stopped, and asked the pocket question out loud. "What's the brave thing, and what's the silly thing?"

image.light: night on the road; stars, and the lantern's tiny blue glow
image.ember: sitting close, looking up at the eldest
image.comfort_in_frame: hands held, Ember's tail round their feet

pictures.text: Ember wouldn't choose the way on, so [[child:eldest]] took a lantern breath. [[block:ch3.p22b]] It was an old milestone, with one side still, out of the wind.

image.setting: a low grey milestone by the road, a little lantern carved on top
image.light: night on the road; stars, and the lantern's tiny blue glow
image.ember: sniffing the still side of the stone

pictures.text: [[block:pic3.p26]] The blue flame flickered and bowed, like someone very tired, but it stayed steady.

image.light: night on the road; stars, and the lantern's tiny blue glow

figures.doing: holding an invisible lantern up high, one step forward

props: the lantern with its tiny blue flame
image.ember: sitting on the still side, tail round her paws

pictures.text: [[block:ch3.p21]] [[child:eldest]] set the lantern down in the lee. Everyone made a wall, hands on knees.

image.light: night on the road; stars, and the lantern's tiny blue glow

figures.doing: setting the lantern down on the grass
kneeling, back to the wind, hands on knees

props: the lantern in the stone's shelter, its tiny blue flame standing straight
image.ember: wrapping her tail round the youngest
image.comfort_in_frame: everyone tucked close in the stone's shelter

pictures.text: [[block:pic3.end]] "Someone I know walked this road tonight," said Ember. The flame was only a blue bead. Would it hold till morning?

image.setting: the lee of the milestone, under the stars
image.light: night on the road; stars, and the lantern's tiny blue glow

figures.doing: kneeling, back to the wind, hands on knees

props: the lantern on the grass with its tiny blue flame
image.ember: curled round the youngest, nose lifted to the wind
image.comfort_in_frame: everyone huddled together, tucked in the fox's tail

Lantern up!", the eldest's middle-way line and key act in the lee, Ember's clue and the canon's closing hook. Nothing new happens.

No sentence over 15 words. Two pictures carry four sentences (11 and 12); the rest carry three.
Each picture has at most one speaker (Should).
"steady" said three times (pictures 5 and 10), shown in the eldest's careful carrying and the flame standing up in the lee.

Same markers as the master. Grandparent lines sit in blocks (pic3.p2.gp, ch3.p5.gp, pic3.p10.gp, pic3.p13.gp); the youngest's and middle child's lines sit in family-size blocks (pic3.small, ch3.p22b, pic3.p26, pic3.end); the eldest's middle-way line reuses the master's access block ch3.p21.

Every picture is pinned to one master paragraph; youngest_act (picture 9, p25), pause_and_ask (picture 8, p19, where the Pause & ask sits) and comfort_final (picture 12, last) each sit on exactly one picture. Picture 1 starts with the legend slot; the jar picture (6) has the role "jar", is pinned to jar.p8 and ends with the jar_credit slot.
Pictures 7 to 11 are at dusk or night; each shows comfort in the frame (hands held, Ember pressed close, everyone together).

Setting, light, figures by slot left to right, feelings in bodies, props, Ember's pose and framing; no child's looks; nothing on the never-drawn list (only the grandparent holds the open lantern; the names on the base and the milestone show no readable letters; nobody in water). Each 80 words or fewer.

flags_for_jon: No scene_art_notes exist for Part 1 (the part sheet has no such field), so the pictures' look comes from part-01's "place" line and the master: honey-gold hearth light indoors, low gold then orange sun on the road, then night blue with stars and the lantern's tiny blue glow. Suggest prompt 1c add a scene_art_notes field so all five Part 1 chapters draw from one note.

Canon §8's picture-book layout (N2) shows a "Last time" line on the picture-book page. 1e's schema has no field for it and the first picture must start with the legend slot, so no "Last time" line is in the picture text; suggest the app shows the master's opening_block.last_time above picture 1, as the N2 layout does.

Kit wording: 1e says the "For the youngest" prompt sits at the youngest's act picture, but the schema nests it in pause_and_ask_simple with the Pause & ask picture's number (and the checker wants that). Kept as the schema. The talk prompt ("What color is the little flame now?") answers the same at pictures 8 and 9, since the flame is a blue bead in both.

The master marks two youngest acts: "Please" as the flame is given (p3) and "Big stone!" at the crisis (p25). The youngest_act role goes to "Big stone!" (picture 9, p25), the act that changes what happens; "Please" has its own picture (2). The key act is the eldest's, so the checker confirms this pin by judgment.

Simplified for one speaker a picture and four sentences at most: Ember's clue is "Someone I know walked this road tonight" (canon: "Someone else walked this road tonight. Someone I know."), and "Who?" and "Sleep now." are left out. The eldest's middle-way line rides with the key act in picture 11 (pinned to p35), so the brave choice and the act sit together. Left out of the words (kept in the master): Ember's fib-sneeze, the old law of the road, and "That is my tail, and I should like it back." The laugh is Ember stepping round every puddle, and her wind-blown tail in picture 7's image.

The favorite-animal slot in the jar default (jar.p3) is neither named in picture 6's words nor drawn, so a family's own favorite never contradicts the picture. Drawing a family's favorite would need a Tier C picture.

For the variants step (1f): pic3.p26 ("I'll help… Lantern up!") and pic3.small ("whispered") have no access versions. The master's own gesture block (ch3.p26) is too long for the 15-word cap, so pic3.p26 needs signs and talker versions of its own. The two picture blocks no picture uses now (pic3.p1.gp and pic3.p22b) were removed from s1-ch03.blocks.json, since picture 9 uses the master's ch3.p22b, which has the access versions.
